subject: Immediate: Cloudwave throughput suppression — policy misalignment and exec action
messages:
From: James Liu <james@cloudwave.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-24T08:32:00Z
Subject: Spike in latency / 429s on production — urgent

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing a sharp drop in throughput and a spike in 429s starting ~08:30 UTC this morning. Our UI calls to your API are returning 429 or timing out; latency has climbed from ~120ms p95 to >2s and our error rate is about 18% across yesterday's baseline. Throughput for our primary route dropped from ~5k RPS to ~800 RPS.

This is impacting live customers and payments flows. We tried to scale on our side but the failures are consistent. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your rate-limiting or burst policies for our account in the last 12 hours?

Attached: brief trace snippets and our client-side error sample (support_logs.zip). Please advise next steps — this is P1 for us.

Thanks,
James Liu
Head of Platform, Cloudwave Labs
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>

James — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're treating this as P1. I've looped in Karthik (rate-limiting) and Connor (infra) to triage immediately.

Quick asks while we investigate: can you send the last 15m of request IDs (x-request-id) and confirm whether you saw any large burst events from your side around 08:25–08:35 UTC?

We'll report back within 30 minutes with an initial hypothesis and immediate mitigations.

—Rachel

To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-24T09:29:03Z
Subject: Fwd: Spike in latency / 429s on production — Cloudwave (P1): quick context and attachments

Team — forwarding Cloudwave's report. Key facts:
- Start: ~2026-06-24 08:30 UTC
- Observable: p95 latency >2s, error rate ~18%, throughput fall to ~800 RPS for their primary route
- Customer impact: payments UI failing for some customers (they flagged outages)

Attachments I've pulled from their first note: support_logs.zip and a short traffic dump (traffic_snapshot.json). Also attaching the current token bucket config we have for their account: token_bucket_config.yaml.

Immediate asks: can you validate whether our safety-valve or an autoscale policy triggered a change that would suppress their tokens? Karthik — can you check the quota window alignment (seconds vs ms) and the burst refill schedule for this account? Connor — can infra confirm whether any routing policy or circuit breaker fired at 08:25–08:40?

If this looks like a policy misconfiguration we'll need a short exec note and an ask for temporary capacity reservation.

Rachel
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-24T10:01:18Z
Subject: RE: Fwd: Spike in latency / 429s on production — Cloudwave (P1): initial triage

Quick update from rate-limiter side: I pulled the policy changes and token accounting for Cloudwave. Initial findings:
- At 09:00 UTC a global safety-valve rule was deployed that tightened burst windows for lower-tier customers. Cloudwave's account was unexpectedly matched by a selector because their dedicated routing label was missing (label drift).
- The token bucket window for their profile was configured as 1000ms in our staging DSL, but the runtime interpreted it as 1s vs the intended 1,000ms transformation done during a refactor — effectively shrinking the refill cadence and causing token starvation under sustained short bursts.
- We also observed the burst TTL reset triggered a refill suppression when consecutive small bursts occurred — a logic regression in the refill guard.

Immediate mitigations I'm proposing:
1) Elevate Cloudwave to emergency throughput tier (temporary quota bump) — low-risk and will restore productive flow in ~2 minutes.
2) Roll back the safety-valve selector that incorrectly matched their routing labels.
3) Patch the refill-guard regression in next hotfix and schedule a canary.

Connor — can you execute (1) and (2) now? I'll prepare a short exec ask for temporary capacity and credits.

Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Executive Team <execs@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-24T11:15:00Z
Subject: EXEC BRIEF: Cloudwave Labs — production suppression due to policy selector drift (action requested)

TL;DR: Cloudwave's production traffic was suppressed this morning due to a safety-valve deployment that inadvertently matched their account (label drift) combined with a refill cadence regression. The customer experienced elevated latency, widespread 429s, and reduced throughput.

Impact: visible to customers (payments UI), estimated affected sessions: ~2.1k over the 30m window, customer-facing SLA risk.

Request: approval for a 48-hour emergency capacity reservation (Dedicated capacity slot) and a goodwill credit of two days of committed usage to Cloudwave while we complete RCA and patch. Estimated 48-hour incremental cost: $18k.

Action already taken: Connor applied the temporary quota bump and removed the mis-matching safety-valve selector (traffic restored as of 10:12 UTC). Karthik is preparing the patch; patch deploy target: 2026-06-24 18:00 UTC with canary.

Docs and evidence: action plan + timeline: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Aq9-example-action-plan
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4821 (for any commercial follow-up).

Please reply with APPROVE/DECLINE. If APPROVE, finance will be looped to provision the 48-hour slot and apply a temporary credit.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability

Best,
James
